brief: JPM's Oct 13 morning briefing: breadth stayed supportive (over 60% of S&P 500 higher) even as all three indices closed lower, with declines concentrated in AI-linked semis and memory. Drivers cited: Broadcom CEO Hock Tan warned financing could become a bigger AI bottleneck than component shortages, a weekend note reignited power-shortage worries (up to 19GW next year), and CXMT's memory announcement added to the pressure. Oil reversed yesterday's gains this morning after a weekend escalation (Houthi attack on a Saudi airport, Russia hitting Ukrainian energy sites despite a ceasefire) had added upside risk to crude. JPM's factor desk flagged tightening macro conditions lifting Quality, with semis sentiment above the 99th percentile, and sees meaningful reversal risk around CPI and the Fed meeting if the Fed turns dovish. For Q3 earnings, FactSet expects 12.4% revenue growth and 29.6% earnings growth for the S&P 500, decelerating from Q2's 52.3% earnings growth; all 11 sectors are expected to grow both metrics, only the second time ever. JPM reiterates a Tactically Bullish equity stance into earnings, viewing recent Semis weakness as a wall of worry it can climb, citing Hynix/Samsung earnings strength, with risks including a tech unwind, AI credit fears, and weaker consumer data.
